text:
Cutter Gauthier is the reason people outside Southern California are watching the Ducks. Fourteen goals in seven games put him next to Mario Lemieux and Alexander Mogilny in the record book, and his last ten games read 19 points on chances worth about 10.7. That is a hot streak sitting on top of a real scorer, and the Ducks need every bit of it.

Because the team underneath is a coin flip. Anaheim is 10-9-1 with 21 points, and at five on five it has taken 46% of the expected goals (the quality of chances, not just the count). It is finishing almost eight goals above its chances and its goalies are giving almost eight back. The Granlund, Gauthier and Beckett Sennecke line has outscored teams 7-4 while getting only 42% of the chances, which is fun until it isn't. Five penalties a game doesn't help.

The worry is in net. Lukas Dostal is at .832 and 4.5 goals worse than expected over his last five starts, while Laurent Brossoit has strung together wins. Whoever holds the crease decides whether the scoring is enough.

Our playoff odds sit at 53%, about as undecided as a number gets. What we'd watch next: whether Tristan Luneau's 12 points in ten survives the cooling we expect, and how much more rope 6'5" rookie Roger McQueen gets.
